To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the engagement of Fas-mediated caspasemediated caspase cleavages and the engagement of TRAIL-mediated apoptosis in primary salivary gland cells in primary Sjoegren’s syndrome are regulated by the induction of type II cells.

Fas-mediated type II cells and TRAIL-mediated apoptosis in primary SGEC are regulated by PI3K and caspase 8 activation, and that TRAIL-induced caspas-9 activation and cytochrome C release in SGEC are independent of the Fas signaling.
TRAIL-mediated type 2 cells in apoptosis of salivary gland cells in pSS were induced rapidly and strongly, which was not mediated by Fas-mediated apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of apoptosis by anti-Fas and TRAIL.
the induction of TRAIL and anti-Fas antibody-mediated apoptosis in SGEC.
the expression of Fas and Fas ligand in the primary salivary gland of patients with Sjögren syndrome and the role of Fas and caspase 8 in the pathogenesis of Sjögren's syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fas-mediated apoptosis was induced in the presence or absence of PI3K inhibitor.
the expression of the effector proteins of the Fas-mediated pathway is induced by the activation of Fas in SGEC of pSS.
the induction of apoptosis in primary cultured cells from the salivary glands of pSS patients is regulated by the type II cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of Fas and Fas ligand (FasL) in SGEC was not sufficient for the induction of apoptosis.
the Fas-mediated apoptosis was induced in SGEC in pSS by the PI3K pathway.
the expression of the death receptor ligand TRAIL and the expression of the effector molecule Apaf-1 are upregulated in primary cultured SGCEC from patients with pSS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TRAIL is more potent than Fas in induction of apoptosis in SGEC of patients with pSS.

the death receptor-mediated apoptosis of primary cultured salivery gland epithelial cells in patients with pSS is regulated by the activation of type II cells, which is not observed in healthy subjects.
TRAIL-induced type II cells are more effective than Fas-mediated type I cells in apoptosis of salivary gland cells.
